Formaldehyde is readily soluble in water, and a 40% aqueous solution of formal- dehyde called formalin is used to preserve biological specimens. It is a component of wood smoke and helps to preserve smoked meat and fish, probably by reacting with nitrogen-containing groups in the proteins of attacking bacteria. Its major use is in making polymer adhesives and insulating foam.

The simplest ketone is acetone, in which two methyl groups are bonded to the central carbon. The bonding scheme is the same as that shown in Figure 7.23, with alkyl or aromatic groups replacing hydrogen atoms in the two single bonds. Such compounds can be prepared by dehydrogenation or oxidation of secondary alcohols, just as aldehydes come from primary alcohols.
